provenance.what: Eleventh live run: both golden sets with model calls queued to the slots the endpoint actually has. llama.py had claimed the app 'serializes its requests through the cascade anyway' - an assumption about one person using a laptop, with no lock, semaphore or queue anywhere in the cascade, the providers or the API. The enterprise direction (many laptops, one company server) rests on it being true. Measured against a real single-slot llama-server, four simultaneous questions: one answered, three refused, three streams severed - and each refusal told the asker no model was reachable and their configuration was at fault, when nothing was misconfigured. The same four asked one at a time: four answers. With the gate: four of four, zero severed streams, 77s wall clock against 51s to fail.
provenance.models: Chat: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M via llama-cpp-python, one slot. Embeddings: nomic-embed-text v1.5 Q4_K_M, task prefixes applied.
provenance.corpus: evals/corpus/aveline in full (11 documents); companion run on the repository documents/
provenance.hardware: 4-core CPU container, no GPU; both model servers local
provenance.caveat: These sets ask their questions one at a time, so they cannot exercise the gate at all - they are here to show it changed no answer, which is the only thing they can honestly say about it. The concurrency behaviour is measured by the live before/after above and pinned by tests/test_concurrency.py, which asserts in both directions: six simultaneous questions must all be answered with the gate, and must fail without it, since a fake endpoint that quietly queued would make the passing test meaningless.
